lines.caleb-intro: So this is Caleb. He's a pipefitter, and he doesn't have a work email… so he signs in with his personal email and a code.
lines.caleb-portal: He started on September twentieth. He's already done the first course, and the second one's due October fourth.
lines.setup: Okay, here's how I set that up. It's one program, with three Skillsoft courses.
lines.schedule: I turn on the release schedule, and it counts from each person's start date.
lines.days: Day zero, day seven, day fourteen… and seven days to finish each one.
lines.rule-intro: Then, who gets it. If you've been building a separate grouping for every release… here it's one rule.
lines.conditions: Field Operations, started on or after September first.
lines.all-four: All four get it… and new field hires get picked up after onboarding.
lines.preview: If I put in Caleb's start date, September twentieth… those are his dates. Due the twenty-seventh, due October fourth, and the last one opens October fourth.
lines.caleb-done-v2: And now he's done two of three. He's caught up… the last one opens October fourth.
lines.overdue: And in the overview, Luis is in the same program, and he's behind on all three. It shows how late he is, and which rule assigned them.
lines.no-deadline: And this is the 'Nothing will chase them' list. Owen has a course with no due date, so nothing's going to follow up on it.
lines.outro: So I set it up once… and every new field hire gets it on their own schedule.
